correction_reason: The previous other_fine_fraction pooled ANY of many different birds, while own_fine_fraction used one focal bird. The revised metric compares focal repeated fine subcell occupancy to one other individual sampled uniformly from eligible birds with non-target-date coarse-cell observations.
revision_of_previous_interpretation: DO NOT compare focal 54.9/47.1% to pooled-any 70.8/75.0% and infer focal routes are less recurrent. Those denominators differ. Equal-bird other rates are 24.9/29.2%.
method: Only x-y, speed, date, bird ID and archived source quality flags; 50km fixed coarse and 5km nested subcells, all original stage rosters frozen, no GPS altitude field opened. Each bird-day and bird weighted equally. A candidate other bird needs at least one non-target-date observation in same coarse cell.

supported: Focal migratory storks in both cohorts re-use the same 5km fine subcell within the eligible 50km corridor across days more often than a uniformly weighted eligible other bird, conditional on original source visitation/sampling.

Only 2013 had a precommitted positive centered height-shape identity test; 2014 did not, despite positive relative fine-route recurrence. Fine horizontal recurrence alone is insufficient to guarantee altitude-identity gain.

In 2013, relative fine route recurrence and previously fixed per-bird raw altitude identity gain are positively associated in post-outcome diagnostics; 2014 association is directionally positive but small-n inference weak.
unsupported: Fine route fidelity causes high altitude shape individuality.
Source-level magnitude 30.0 vs 17.9 points differs significantly; interval includes zero.
2014 significant route-gain association: bird-bootstrap95 includes zero and posthoc age-group p=0.0953.
The 2013 posthoc p=0.0426 is an independent prespecified confirmatory test; multiple exploratory metrics and result-aware question invalidate such interpretation.
Other-bird equalization solves all effort bias: other birds still have different number of fixes/days and tracking quality.
Fine route recurrence measures actual repeated atmospheric uplift, food or competitor availability.
2013 and 2014 independently establish identical individual-specific wind responses.

new_biological_question: Which landscape/atmospheric and behavioural conditions allow repeatable horizontal routes to become repeatable VERTICAL distributions? Test in a new source after matching true micro-location, available uplift and device errors.
